messages.content:
Sarunyu has a stick of length 1 with one endpoint marked in red. Every minute, he picks one of his sticks uniformly at random and breaks it into two halves of equal length. Compute the expected length of the stick with the red endpoint after 5 minutes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(L_m\) be the length of the red-marked stick after \(m\) minutes, with \(L_0=1\).

At minute \(m\), there are \(m\) sticks total, and exactly one of them contains the red endpoint. Since Sarunyu chooses a stick uniformly at random, the probability he chooses the red stick at minute \(m\) is

\[
\frac1m.
\]

If he chooses it, its length is halved; otherwise it stays the same. Therefore, conditioning on the past,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_m \mid \text{past}]
=
\frac1m \cdot \frac{L_{m-1}}2
+
\left(1-\frac1m\right)L_{m-1}
=
\left(1-\frac1{2m}\right)L_{m-1}.
\]

Taking expectations gives

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_m]
=
\left(1-\frac1{2m}\right)\mathbb{E}[L_{m-1}].
\]

Thus

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
=
\prod_{m=1}^5 \left(1-\frac1{2m}\right)
=
\left(\frac12\right)\left(\frac34\right)\left(\frac56\right)\left(\frac78\right)\left(\frac9{10}\right).
\]

So

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
=
\frac{1\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 9}{2\cdot 4\cdot 6\cdot 8\cdot 10}
=
\frac{945}{3840}
=
\frac{63}{256}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{63}{256}}
\]
